curator_note: Classic Nigerian just off Oxford Street: jollof, egusi with pounded yam, suya.
Fine-dining West African tasting menu. Pan-regional rather than purely Nigerian.
Family-run Ethiopian in Camberwell for big injera platters, with a coffee ceremony. Hours vary, so check.
Ethiopian kitchen with coffee ceremony and monthly cultural nights.
Long-running Eritrean spot reopened under new management; serves Eritrean and Ethiopian.
Brixton spot serving Eritrean and Ethiopian food together, so not a pure Eritrean pick.
Sabiib's second site (June 2025). Haniid lamb shoulder with sabaayad. Fully halal.
Original Sabiib (June 2023). Mogadishu-inspired décor. Haniid and suqaar stars. Halal, alcohol-free.
Riverside steakhouse owned by a Stellenbosch wine estate: SA wines, biltong, malva pudding. Food mostly European. Weekdays only.
Family-run Mauritian: dholl puri, bowl renverse, curries. Closed Tuesdays.
Mauritian street food in Leyton, formerly Mauritian Delights: dhall puri, biryani, curries. Walk-ins; reportedly cash only.
Jamaican diner with a jerk pit, curry goat and rum cocktails, plus live reggae. Second site after Camden.
London's first Caribbean diner (2015): jerk wings, rum cocktails and reggae.
Trinidadian roti shop: doubles, aloo pie, curry goat. Takeaway. Two addresses reported; phone ahead.
Peruvian: ceviche, lomo saltado, causa and pisco. Closed Mon-Tue.
Peruvian and Nikkei (Japanese-Peruvian) small plates with pisco bar at Kingly Court.
Venezuelan arepas, cachapas and empanadas on gluten-free corn. Street-food style, with sister sites around London.
Venezuelan arepas and cachapas by Regent's Canal. Famous weekend brunch.
Family Colombian started by Lalo (2010). Bandeja paisa, empanadas, patacones. Now Brixton Hill.
Tiny Argentine parrilla since 2004. Charcoal-grilled steaks and Argentine wine list.
Family-run Argentine parrilla since 2010: charcoal-grilled beef, empanadas, sorrentinos. Evenings; weekends from noon.
Santiago Lastra's regional Mexican, just off Regent Street. Opened October 2024.
Long-running regional Mexican with tequila and mezcal. Chelsea branch also.
Family-run Georgian in Stoke Newington: khinkali, khachapuri, wine. Opened early 2026.
Georgian with qvevri amber wines. Kensington branch; sister in Pimlico. Closed Monday lunch.
Long-running Armenian family cafe. The menu mixes Armenian, Persian and Middle Eastern dishes, so a looser fit.
Cosy Azerbaijani near King's Cross: piti, levengi, plov. Closed Mondays; weekday evenings only. Phone ahead.

address: 2 Central Parade, Streatham High Rd, London
curator_note: Homemade Uzbek plov, manti, samsa and hand-pulled lagman. Moved from Queensway/Bayswater.
Chef Muzaffar Sadykov's Uzbek: plov, lagman, manti. Vegan options. Grab-and-go by day.
Uzbek in Bow: plov, samsa, lagman and manti. HMC halal. Book via WhatsApp.
Burmese specialist in The Yards: tea leaf salad, mohinga.
Burmese restaurant and deli on Bermondsey Street near London Bridge. Closed Sundays.
Filipino all-day diner and bakery from Romulo Cafe team. Family-style plates, ube.

address: 2.14 Top Floor, Kingly Court, Carnaby St, London
curator_note: Modern Filipino at Kingly Court. Closed Mondays; book ahead.
Filipino grill (inihaw) in Charlton. Dine-in and takeaway. Closed Wednesdays.
Modern halal Malaysian in Bayswater. Nasi lemak, beef rendang wagyu and roti.
Halal Singaporean-Malay food (nasi ambeng, rendang, satay), opened April 2026. Not strictly Malaysian, so a curator call.
Original Soho location. Sri Lankan hoppers, kothu and roasts. Some South Indian dosas.
Sri Lankan street food: hoppers, kothu, devilled plates and arrack cocktails.
Casual Nepali counter: momos, thukpa, chowmein and curries.
Lao menu from Rosa's Thai team. Char-grilled meats, herbs and curries. Listed as Thai, but Lao.

restaurant: Heng Heng at The Red Cow
curator_note: Cambodian and Thai kitchen inside the Red Cow pub, so a curator exception to the specialist rule.
Original BAO (2015). Modern Taiwanese: gua bao and small plates. Walk-ins only.

address: Unit R04, 11 St Giles Square, London
curator_note: Taiwanese dumpling chain famous for xiao long bao. Book ahead.
Long-running Hoxton institution since 2002. Pho and banh mi on Kingsland Road Pho Mile.
Vietnamese in Hoxton, formerly Ant House. Pho, banh mi, sizzling plates and street food.
Family-run Polish in Acton: pierogi, żurek, golabki. Closes early.
Polish classics in the Polish Hearth Club townhouse. Central and Eastern European menu, house vodkas.
Hungarian and Romanian menu near Leyton Midland Road: goulash and more. Shared cuisine; Lakehouse is the purer pick.
Sibling-run Hungarian in South Woodford. Dine-in first and last weekend of month only.
Homely Romanian: sarmale, mamaliga, Moldavian tochitura on Green Lanes.
Small Romanian-run in Leyton. Seafood-led menu with Romanian dishes like sarmale.
Ukrainian in Shoreditch with open kitchen. Recipes from Tatarbunary, southern Ukraine. Book SevenRooms.
Independent Ukrainian bar and grill (former Alchemist). Borscht, chicken Kyiv, varenyky. Live music.
Contemporary Portuguese in Fitzrovia. Closed Sundays; Monday dinner only.
Algarve piri-piri chicken on wood charcoal grill, hidden bar. By Borough Market.

address: Great Scotland Yard Hotel, 3-5 Great Scotland Yard, London
curator_note: Niklas Ekstedt's open-fire cooking: Nordic technique, British produce, Swedish chef. Pricey, and not strictly Swedish.
Afghan charcoal grill: kabuli platter and feast platters. 100% halal. Some Mediterranean starters.
Afghan grill on Brick Lane. Chapli kebabs, lamb karahi. Dine-in, takeaway and delivery.
Yemeni mandi and haneeth with floor seating on Edgware Road.
Newer Yemeni: mandi, haneeth, zurbian, malawah. Table or floor seating. Halal.
Modern Palestinian from chef Fadi Kattan. Opened December 2022.
Takeaway Palestinian. Sister site is mandi-focused, so menu may lean Yemeni.
Iraqi and Kurdish grill: kebabs and big portions. Kurdish-leaning rather than purely Iraqi.
Iraqi speciality: masgouf (grilled carp) needs pre-ordering. Also quzi and kubbah.
Long-running Ghanaian chop bar: jollof, waakye, banku, fufu with soups. Good food, slow service; a better pick is wanted.
Brazilian rodizio steakhouse chain (curator exception).
Family-owned Indonesian near Covent Garden for 30+ years: rendang, sate, nasi goreng. Menu leans Indonesian-Malaysian.
